allowList.reason: dev-switch/dev-server ids are also referenced by cable-uplink's a_device_id/b_device_id, which the cables->connections migration (#3091) consumes when resolving the endpoint's PlacedPort. The device ids themselves are retained on the devices; this only satisfies the count-based silent-loss check's coincidental value reuse, not an actual loss.

Uplink 1 / NIC 1 interface names are also referenced by cable-uplink's a_interface/b_interface, consumed by the migration to resolve the matching PlacedPort by template_name. The InterfaceTemplate.name and PlacedPort.template_name fields themselves are retained unchanged (same collision caveat as above).

The legacy cables array is fully consumed by the read-path migration (#3091). id is replaced by a freshly minted connection id (never reused, to avoid colliding with an id minted elsewhere). a_device_id/a_interface and b_device_id/b_interface are resolved to PlacedPort ids and are not stored verbatim on the Connection. type has no Connection equivalent and is intentionally dropped. cable-orphan's label is discarded because neither of its endpoints resolves (dev-ghost-a/dev-ghost-b do not exist), so the whole cable is dropped; cable-uplink's label and color do carry over onto the migrated connection and are not part of this loss.
